subject: physics

verification.note: Asked in TS Inter I-Year Physics Paper-I, March 2016 (Q1) and March 2024 (Q1) — Section A, 2 marks each time. The 1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it; the question text itself is sourced from those papers. `appearances` is deliberately left empty — a separate reviewed tagging pass fills it, and a hand-written tag here would be an invented claim. Content hand-checked against NCERT Class-11 Chapter 1: physics is the study of the basic laws of nature and their manifestation in different natural phenomena, studied in a macroscopic domain (laboratory, terrestrial and astronomical scales) and a microscopic domain (atoms, nuclei and elementary particles).

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The definition
lines: Physics is the study of the basic laws of
nature and the way those laws show
A small number of laws accounts for a
steps.margin_note: First mark. One sentence of definition. Do not list chapter names.
steps.why: Physics is defined by what it looks for, not by a list of topics: a small set of laws that hold everywhere, and the many different phenomena those same few laws produce.
common_mistakes: Listing topics — mechanics, heat, light — instead of giving a definition. A list is not a definition.

recall.must_convey: That physics is the study of the basic laws of nature and how they show themselves in natural phenomena.
accept: study of nature and its laws

steps.memory_tip: Few laws, many phenomena. That contrast is the whole definition in four words.

steps.label: The two domains
lines: Physics is studied in two domains:
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Name both domains, with one example of scale for each.
steps.why: The two domains are separated by the size of the objects studied, and different laws dominate in each — classical mechanics and thermodynamics in the macroscopic domain, quantum theory in the microscopic one.
common_mistakes: Naming only one domain. Two marks means the definition and both domains.

recall.must_convey: That physics has a macroscopic domain and a microscopic domain.

steps.memory_tip: Two domains split by size: laboratory up to stars, and atoms down to particles.

insider_note: Two marks means two things: one sentence of definition and both domains named. A list of chapter names earns neither.
